title: MADGER - Living Places
scope: Thirteen furnished landmark ground floors, local histories and story opportunities within the existing fourteen-community world. Two complete companion stories deepen relationships. This additive volume does not replace the world atlas.
chronology_rule: Local history additions are writer canon. Scene seeds and the two short stories are authored possible episodes; their placement is provisional until a dated episode ledger adopts them. They do not silently change pilot knowledge.

landmarks.name: Reedbank Kitchen
landmarks.history: The kitchen began as a ferry-workers meal fund, long after Reedbank itself was founded. Households contributed labor as often as money. The building survived several ordinary floods because its raised floor was maintained, not because the river spared deserving people. Seven years before the pilot, its dry rooms became temporary shelter. Afterward, the volunteers copied the flood height onto a removable measuring board: the room itself was not flooded to that height. Some families remember generous depot deliveries; others remember the prices that followed. Both memories are true. Dara keeps the serving rota beside the donations ledger so a wealthy name cannot erase a month of unpaid work.
landmarks.daily_life: Before dawn, kitchen workers arrive through the normal entrance and carry ingredients along the passage. Breakfast is served from a movable cart in the common room; cooking remains in the separate kitchen. Upper guest rooms are occupied by travelers and visiting relatives. At midday, children copy recipes while adults repair river baskets. A red token means a bowl has already been paid for; nobody receiving it must explain why. The dry measuring board is brought out only for Watermark Night.
landmarks.conflict: Veyra offers to replace the worn tables if her depot receives exclusive supply rights. Refusing leaves a real expense; accepting would weaken the kitchen’s independence. Dara favors a slower public subscription. Hollis worries that pride can also become an excuse to let people go hungry. Their disagreement is affectionate, practical and unresolved until the actual bids are compared.
landmarks.scene_seed: At Watermark Night, a child paints a flood line too high. Hollis starts to correct it, then asks whose memory the child followed. The answer belongs to a house on a lower wharf. The kitchen adds the house datum to the board instead of declaring one family wrong. Madger learns that a shared record must preserve where each witness stood.
landmarks.material_direction: Raised timber floor, pale lime plaster, dark beams, ochre ceramics, blue-gray river light and warm task lamps. No water or river channel inside the common room.

landmarks.name: White Family Workshop
landmarks.history: The White family workshop belongs to the working terrace, not to a heroic dynasty. Its benches have been shortened, widened and patched for successive users. Nine years before the pilot, the platform failure injured Eris and exposed Gorilla’s refusal to call a halt. The failed platform was at a worksite, not secretly beneath this floor. The workshop later adopted a stop-board beside its tool checkout: any worker can suspend a task and record a reason. Eris recovered, adapted her methods and became a crew lead. Her brother’s guilt is only one part of her life; she also competes in terrible music contests and dislikes visitors who turn every conversation into an inquiry about her hand.
landmarks.daily_life: Stone fitting is prepared in the bench room and assembled across the passage. The tool store closes at shift end, while the wash/office remains available for handover notes. Dust collection is a maintained work practice, never a magical absence of dust. Meals happen away from the cutting benches. A half-built percussion frame is a voluntary evening project, and nobody is allowed to conscript an apprentice into finishing it.
landmarks.conflict: A donor wants Gorilla’s name placed above the workshop door. Eris wants the money for better shared equipment but refuses to make the place a monument to someone who lives elsewhere. Oren believes the practical benefit matters more than the sign. Gorilla must ask what help is wanted and accept an answer smaller than a grand rescue.
landmarks.scene_seed: Gorilla offers to carry a loaded workbench alone. Eris asks him to hold a measuring cord while an apprentice marks the floor. He can do it perfectly, yet feels useless. The scene turns when he notices the apprentice is afraid to question a measurement and invites the objection before Eris has to.
landmarks.material_direction: Cut limestone walls, dark timber, copper roof weathering, pale stone dust, rust-red work cloths. Warm side light; no forge or open furnace in this household workshop.

landmarks.name: Six Roads Inn
landmarks.history: The Six Roads name is a supper custom, not evidence that six new highways enter Latchford. The town grew around three roads; the inn later named six tables for six common onward destinations. During the Severance, households took turns hosting stranded travelers, and the custom outlived the emergency. A generation ago the inn introduced a departure book with corrections written visibly beneath the original entry. This made it less elegant and more useful. Asha cooked for convoys here before retirement. Sela still trusts the room, but her concealed evacuation funding has not yet become public at the pilot baseline.
landmarks.daily_life: Arrivals leave wet gear on freestanding racks before entering the common room. Supper seats people by destination. Sleeping quarters remain private; a meal token does not purchase access to a guest’s route notes. Dispatch work belongs to the convoy house and relay offices elsewhere. Snow’s familiar resting mat can be placed beneath the common-room side table when Asha visits. It is removed and stored after her stay, not permanently installed as a shrine.
landmarks.conflict: An innkeeper can protect a traveler’s privacy while still warning about an unsafe route. Sela sometimes confuses useful discretion with the secrecy that protected her own decision. Asha notices the distinction but will not expose another person’s history as dinner entertainment. The room allows a confrontation to begin with a practical question rather than an accusation.
landmarks.scene_seed: One place remains set for a delayed traveler. Sela offers to buy the unused meal. Asha refuses to call it unused until the route steward checks the arrival yard. Snow hears a familiar harness buckle before anyone sees its owner. The delay proves ordinary, but the argument reveals which characters assume absence means abandonment.
landmarks.material_direction: Warm timber arcades, blue convoy cloth, terracotta cups, rain-dark stone at the threshold. A hospitable rectangular room; no new tunnel, hidden hatch or indoor road.

landmarks.name: Varr Workshop
landmarks.history: Varr Workshop grew from a cooperative making canal instruments and repair tools. Eight years before the pilot, its members built Bot’s body and supported the sustained learning through which he became a person. The workshop owns its spare components and drawings; it does not own him. His departure for the Burrow five years before the pilot was a choice. Lume saved an early maintenance worksheet because she is sentimental, not because it contains a secret override. The canal flood that shaped Nix’s distrust affected a different part of Millmere’s civic history. Bot’s origin and Nix’s grievance overlap in place without becoming one hidden master plot.
landmarks.daily_life: Morning work begins with tool calibration in the bench room. Projects enter the assembly room only after their owners agree to the scope of repair. The office keeps consent and change records; private notes are not posted on the public job board. A practice instrument occupies one rolling stand. It is mechanically ordinary and often out of tune. Visitors can sit in the assembly room without being measured, scanned or assigned work.
landmarks.conflict: Lume offers Bot a diagnostic check as a gesture of care. Bot wants to visit as a guest. Her hurt is understandable, but it creates no right of access. Their conflict resolves through an agreed narrow task and an evening spent doing something neither can optimize. Nix could exploit the workshop’s reputation, but no magical maker command or ownership claim becomes valid.
landmarks.scene_seed: Bot asks to borrow a tool and Lume reaches for it before asking which one. He waits. She notices, puts it back and lets him describe his own project. His attempt at music produces an ugly buzzing note. Lume laughs only after he does, and the awkward room becomes a shared workshop again.
landmarks.material_direction: Brick, dark timber, brass gauges, painted enamel, canal-reflected light. Friendly practical machinery with physical switches; no operating theater, restraining chair or master control console.

landmarks.name: Seed House
landmarks.chapter_title: A seed is not a promise
landmarks.history: The Seed House developed from Willowmere’s seasonal exchange, after the orchard settlement was already established. Growers first traded surplus in cloth packets; later they recorded harvest conditions on ceramic tags that survived damp storage. A rare seed without its growing history became less valuable than an ordinary seed with a reliable account. The hall’s stalls still belong to rotating contributors, not hereditary vendors. Neri remembers learning here; Sori remembers the labor behind the display. Neither memory makes one of them the rightful owner of the place.
landmarks.daily_life: The central public aisle stays open from end to end. West stalls display dry seeds and growing notes; east stalls hold demonstration trays and tools. Live trials are tended in the existing community gardens rather than turning the hall into an unrecorded greenhouse. Children make impossible plants in clay during the exchange. Bad harvests are entered alongside successes, and a failed packet may remain on display with its explanation.
landmarks.conflict: A merchant wants the most spectacular canopy seed displayed without the warning that it rarely grows outside its native conditions. Sori fears losing the sale; Neri fears teaching a convenient lie. They need an honest demonstration that supports the growers instead of treating commerce and learning as automatic enemies.
landmarks.scene_seed: A child asks why the ugliest clay plant has the longest label. Neri reads its imagined needs; Sori asks who would do that work. The class redesigns the plant together. The joke becomes a practical lesson in how a community supports something beautiful.
landmarks.material_direction: Orchard timber, cream plaster, woven green shades, shallow ceramic drawers, filtered morning sunlight. All stalls remain inside the inherited hall; central aisle unobstructed.

landmarks.name: Workers Hostel
landmarks.chapter_title: The last whistle is not the end
landmarks.history: The hostel stands in the occupied worker district of Cinder Cuts. The freight diversion eighteen years before the pilot reduced paid shifts, but it did not erase the residents or their skills. Families converted short-stay rooms into a mixture of temporary lodging and stable tenancy. Raiders arrived seven years before the pilot and occupied the disused eastern spur, not the entire town. The hostel’s patched furniture records years of ordinary repair. Dreg has relatives in the legitimate neighborhood; this gives him a reason to change, not an excuse for the harm he helps cause.
landmarks.daily_life: At dawn, workers post available hauling and repair jobs. The kitchen serves tenants before taking outside orders. A common-room timetable lists legitimate freight and walking connections; it does not advertise raider patrols. Guests can join the Last Whistle percussion rehearsal using retired, cleaned components. No visitor is required to disclose family ties to stay. Threats are reported through residents’ chosen representatives.
landmarks.conflict: Brakka claims that only her crew provides protection. Residents remember help from some crew members and extortion from others. Kesh must acknowledge that Kettle Crown benefited from the diversion while refusing Brakka’s claim to speak for everyone. Pip can arrange a useful delivery but must reveal his commission before the hostel accepts it.
landmarks.scene_seed: Dreg sees a food crate marked for the hostel among stolen freight. He initially wants to return only that crate. A relative asks why the other families’ names matter less. The scene begins his conflict; it does not erase the need to return goods and testify later.
landmarks.material_direction: Basalt, limewashed repairs, salvaged timber, patched amber lamps and clean kitchen ceramics. Occupied, cared-for rooms; poverty is not rendered as universal filth or villain decoration.

landmarks.name: Bridgewright Pavilion
landmarks.history: Crownrest’s bridgewright practice grew alongside a settlement that moves with living crowns. Early builders tried to keep every connection taut; damage taught later crews to allow measured movement. The pavilion keeps deliberately different sample joints so apprentices can compare their behavior. Its spring position is the registered atlas baseline. Seasonal displacement changes recorded site state rather than silently changing the town map. Senn’s knowledge of a protected route belongs to relationships beyond the workshop; no conveniently hidden map sits in a public drawer.
landmarks.daily_life: Crews check lashings and inspect sample joints before leaving for the bridges. The assembly room builds replaceable sections; full spans are not magically unfolded inside a small room. Dry fiber stays in the tool store. The office records which crown positions a measurement belongs to. A warning chime is a local work signal, not a universal command over trees. Normal conversation and joking continue between inspections.
landmarks.conflict: Festival organizers want a crossing reopened before its movement settles. Senn knows delaying it will cost traders money. Gorilla initially offers more strength and more rope; Senn needs him to keep the waiting crowd from pressuring the inspection crew. A successful defense of the community can mean protecting a careful decision.
landmarks.scene_seed: A child hangs a bell on a sample joint, making every small movement audible. Senn intends to remove it as a distraction, then hears the interval change before he sees the lashing bind. The bell is retained as a teaching aid, with a note that sound alone cannot certify a bridge.
landmarks.material_direction: Living-fiber lashings, dark timber, pale resin repairs, green reflected canopy light. Ordinary interior floor and inherited walls; no giant trunk suddenly occupying the central passage.

landmarks.name: Mirror Observatory
landmarks.history: Ossara’s observatory predates the Severance, but survival did not preserve a perfect archive. Some pages were recopied, some instruments were replaced and some convenient conclusions became tradition. The present public reading room exhibits a damaged measuring plate beside its corrected replacement. Maela learned to value that admission. Kavar sponsors attractive public demonstrations because they build trust; his generosity does not make his water claims accurate. The observatory is not the source of the city’s water and contains no secret aquifer switch.
landmarks.daily_life: Morning readers compare weather notes before the hottest hours. Demonstrations use covered lamps and small mirrors on a screened table; no concentrated beam crosses the public passage. Observing equipment is stored between sessions. The dispatch room schedules public access and communicates findings, while the upper catalogs and ground archives retain their registered uses. Curtains reduce glare without making the room gloomy.
landmarks.conflict: A reflected mark appears to prove that a caravan missed a payment. Maela can explain the optical error, but doing so challenges a respected sponsor. She needs original measurements and witnesses rather than a heroic speech about truth. Kavar can concede one faulty display while continuing to defend the larger debt system.
landmarks.scene_seed: Two visitors stand in different places and insist that a marked disc points in opposite directions. Maela swaps their positions before explaining the reflection. The audience sees the problem before the argument about a disputed record begins.
landmarks.material_direction: Pale sandstone, turquoise shutters, cream linen, brass and dark glass. Warm bounced desert light, controlled bright reflections, no lasers or glowing magical debt machine.

landmarks.name: Rescue Sail House
landmarks.history: The rescue house was established by harbor crews whose families had disagreed over salvage rights for generations. They agreed that rescue should not transfer ownership of a rescued person’s boat or cargo. That principle is posted with actual examples of difficult claims, not a flawless founding legend. The current structure stands on the registered upper refuge datum. The older drowned district and archive are separate places. Toma knows the rescue rule well; his temptation lies in deciding which objects count as abandoned once their owners are hard to find.
landmarks.daily_life: Wet arrivals are assessed in the western shelter. Dry supplies remain in the rear store; gear is cleaned in the guide/wash room before reuse. The eastern shelter gives families a quieter waiting space. Boats moor outside the building’s inherited footprint. A tide board records the last observed level and who measured it, so a copied number is never mistaken for a fresh observation.
landmarks.conflict: A recovered chest contains saleable fittings and papers belonging to a living descendant community. Toma can pay his crew quickly by selling the fittings, but removing them could destroy the evidence that establishes the chest’s origin. Edda insists that care for the rescued crew comes before the ownership hearing; she does not claim authority to settle the hearing herself.
landmarks.scene_seed: A rescued rival tries to repay Toma with a family token. He almost takes it, then asks whether the offer would still be made after a warm meal and a night’s sleep. The pause changes how the crew sees him more than a speech about generosity would.
landmarks.material_direction: Limestone, salt-worn blue timber, coral-colored plaster, rope baskets and strong daylight. Dry refuge interior above the harbor, no wave washing through the room.

landmarks.name: Sailmakers Court
landmarks.chapter_title: The cost of a light thing
landmarks.history: Aurel Quay’s first charter rejected the sale of residents with vessels. Later dock contracts found subtler ways to trap labor through debt and supposedly temporary rescue fees. Sailmakers Court became a place where crews compared those terms alongside their repair work. Its cooperative did not invent liftstone and cannot suspend a ship through willpower. Eri’s expertise is practical: sail condition, weather, loads and the courage to refuse a profitable departure. Serik knows the same craft well enough to disguise exploitation as exceptional service.
landmarks.daily_life: The assembly room holds short sail sections and test frames, not a full ship. Pattern work happens in the bench room; the tool store keeps dry cloth and fittings. Loads are weighed on an ordinary floor scale. Wind checks are taken outside at the existing dock and copied to the office with a time. The hall has solid floors and walls; the cloud sea is visible only through appropriate openings.
landmarks.conflict: A contract promises that rescue charges will end after the next profitable trip, but gives the rescuer control over which trips are allowed. Eri sees the trap. Serik challenges her to offer an immediate alternative. The community must share limited capacity and accept delayed freight, making solidarity a costly choice rather than an easy slogan.
landmarks.scene_seed: During Weight Day, a toy boat wins by carrying less cargo than its label claims. The children laugh until Eri asks what happens when a real captain makes the same substitution. The toy is rebuilt, and its second run is slower but honest.
landmarks.material_direction: Basalt floor, ochre canvas, copper fittings, indigo shadows and high cloud light. Interior scale is modest; no vessel floating inside and no floor opening onto an unguarded abyss.

landmarks.name: Echo Archive
landmarks.history: Hushvale’s archive inherited records of both necessary emergency closures and later abuses of that authority. During the Severance ninety-two years before the pilot, cutting some resonance links prevented a cascade. That true act of protection became a powerful story, and powerful stories attract convenient additions. Echo ice preserves fragments under limited conditions; it does not provide an omniscient recording of history. Ysolde’s training includes identifying gaps. Ossa’s fear is that public uncertainty will reopen a danger she believes the archive alone understands.
landmarks.daily_life: The public room contains ordinary copies and supervised demonstrations. Sensitive originals remain in their registered archive rooms. A cool cabinet protects a small demonstration fragment; the reading room itself is habitable and warm. No one heats an original for a dramatic effect. Visitors can compare transcriptions, including disagreements and uncertainty marks. A demonstration’s limits are explained before a voice is played.
landmarks.conflict: A true warning is attached to a forged continuing prohibition. Rejecting the forgery does not prove the old danger was imaginary. Ysolde needs to separate the claims while Ossa treats separation as disloyalty. Bot must preserve uncertainty and decline a request to infer missing words simply because the crowd wants a complete sentence.
landmarks.scene_seed: An echo repeats a tender phrase with the same breath twice. A visitor hears a loved one; Ysolde hears a copied fragment. She asks permission before explaining the flaw. Respect for grief becomes part of accurate interpretation.
landmarks.material_direction: Limestone, insulated copper fittings, dark wool, blue glacier reflection and warm reading lamps. Small contained ice specimen only; no vast ice wall replacing a room partition.

landmarks.name: Common Kiln Hall
landmarks.history: The Common Kiln Hall coordinates making, inspection and exchange. High-temperature firing takes place in its separately registered kiln annex, not beneath occupied rooms. Kettle Crown prospered after the freight diversion that hurt Cinder Cuts eighteen years before the pilot. Individual makers did not all choose the policy, yet they inherited its advantages. The hall’s public defect shelf began as a way to teach apprentices; it later became a place where makers admitted rushed orders and bad purchasing decisions as well as cracks in clay.
landmarks.daily_life: Greenware is inspected in the bench room before being moved along the clear passage toward its next handling stage. The assembly room packs cooled work. The tool store separates clean supplies from used molds. The wash/office records firing batches and cooperative orders. Cups displayed at the Cooling Feast are fully cooled; nobody handles glowing ceramics as a harmless gag.
landmarks.conflict: A relief order for Cinder Cuts could help residents and also be used as publicity that erases the harm of the diversion. Kesh wants public accounts, fair freight terms and a named residents’ contact. Dreg wants a shortcut that would let his crew take credit. Their negotiation reveals whether he is ready to help without controlling the story.
landmarks.scene_seed: Two makers submit a cup with handles on opposite sides as an absurd festival entry. A resident with a recovering wrist finds it useful. The makers have to decide whether they care more about winning the joke prize or letting someone change the purpose of their work.
landmarks.material_direction: Dark volcanic stone, white clay dust, red ceramics, green garden reflections. Calm cool workroom; the separate hot annex may be implied beyond the exterior, never moved indoors.

landmarks.name: Tide Speakers Hall
landmarks.history: Lumen Tide’s harbor traditions are older than the surface Open Ways and preserve more than one founding account. The Tide Speakers Hall developed as a meeting place among communities with different routes, harvest practices and memories of migration. Its public chart gives travelers useful bearings while withholding nesting-water detail entrusted to particular stewards. This is a living civic practice, not a puzzle whose moral reward is letting a surface hero take the complete map. Namu’s temporary role as a speaker does not make them ruler of the deep city.
landmarks.daily_life: The central aisle serves public circulation and meetings; movable benches are brought from the side bays for a hearing and returned afterward. No fixed dais blocks the north-south route. Fungal produce arrives from the existing exchange and is shared after meetings. A public relief chart stays in a western bay. Restricted route records are held elsewhere under community practice, not hidden behind a secret panel in this hall.
landmarks.conflict: Surface traders offer useful medicine and fittings in exchange for exclusive chart rights. Madger initially thinks a shared copy is a neutral compromise. Namu asks who would enforce its limits after the traders leave. The negotiation must find a service the visitors can contribute without converting hospitality into permanent ownership.
landmarks.scene_seed: A child corrects Toma’s pronunciation of a harbor name. He asks what it means, expecting one neat answer. Two elders disagree and then laugh. The scene establishes a culture with internal variation before outsiders attempt to describe it as a single mysterious people.
landmarks.material_direction: Pale limestone, deep teal textiles, mineral window light, amber lamps and violet fungal accents. Habitable dry hall above the subterranean sea, no underwater breathing or ocean inside the floor.

companion_stories.title: The Unfinished Note
companion_stories.placement: A Stonewake interlude during Gorilla's season-two return. The platform history is already known to the participants; this scene does not replace the separate investigation or bridge opening.
companion_stories.text:
The noise reached the street before Gorilla reached the door. It began as a respectable wooden note, attempted something higher, and collapsed into a sound like a bucket losing an argument.

He stopped with one hand on the lintel.

Inside, Eris struck the instrument again. The same note escaped. She considered it, moved a peg and made it worse.

"You're early," she said.

"I heard something break."

"Then you're exactly on time."

The workshop smelled of cut stone and timber warmed by the afternoon sun. A repaired cord had been borrowed from its stand and hung over the stop-board easel. The bench Gorilla remembered stood in the southwest corner, shortened on one side and raised on blocks. Somebody had painted its legs blue.

He looked at Eris's hand. She looked at his eyes.

"Still attached," she said. "Still mine. Put your bag in the office."

Madger followed him through the south entrance with Snow at his heels. Bot paused beside the instrument frame, amber eyes following the uneven row of wooden bars.

"The third interval is inconsistent."

"So is the fourth," Eris said. "I like to be thorough."

Gorilla set his bag down and began counting useful things. A cracked stool. A fitting bench with one damaged runner. A box too heavy for the young worker trying to move it. The old familiar relief rose in him: here were problems with edges, weight and an answer.

"I'll take that."

The young worker held the box tighter.

Eris did not raise her voice. "He's taking it to the store. You're holding this."

She put the end of a measuring cord in Gorilla's hand.

At the other end, the worker laid a chalk mark for the next assembly. Gorilla could have lifted the entire jig. Instead he held a cord at a penciled cross while someone smaller did the interesting part.

Madger saw the expression and wisely became occupied with Snow's water bowl.

The worker measured twice. On the third pass his ears lowered. He glanced at the board, then at Eris, then at Gorilla.

"Something different?" Gorilla asked.

"Probably me."

Gorilla knew that sentence. He had said it in other forms: only a little strain; one more load; I can hold it until they are clear.

He kept the cord still. "Show us."

The worker pointed to two chalk lines. One belonged to an older revision. Eris rubbed it out, wrote the date beside the new one and handed the chalk back. No one delivered a speech. The room simply continued, with a mistake removed before it became weight.

Later, when the paid work was finished, Gorilla reached for the damaged runner.

Eris put a mallet in his other hand.

"I came to help," he said.

"I noticed. It has been exhausting."

Across the passage, Bot gave a quiet electronic click that might have been amusement.

Eris turned the instrument toward her brother. A row of holes had been drilled at uneven intervals. One had a neat wooden plug in it.

"Wrong place?" Gorilla asked.

"Very confidently wrong."

"I can make a new rail."

"You can play the bad note."

He weighed the mallet in his palm. It was absurdly light.

"Why keep the plug?"

"Because the rail works. Because I have other things to finish. Because a repaired hole is not a prophecy. Pick whichever answer you can survive."

He smiled despite himself. Then the smile went away.

"I should have called the stop."

Eris rested both hands on the bench. Beyond the open room door, a broom moved slowly along the central passage. She waited until it had passed.

"Yes," she said.

The word had no softness in it. It also had no surprise.

"I keep thinking if I'd been stronger—"

"You were strong. That's why everyone believed you when you kept holding it."

He looked down at the mallet.

"I don't need you to win that afternoon again," Eris said. "I need you to notice which afternoon this is."

For a while they listened to the workshop settling around them. A cup touched a saucer in the office. Snow scratched once at her mat, turned twice and lay down.

Gorilla lifted the mallet. "Which bar?"

"The ugly one."

He struck it. The bucket lost its argument again.

Madger laughed so suddenly that Snow raised her head. Bot tilted his own head, listened to the fading vibration, and asked whether the ugliness was now intentional.

"It was always intentional," Eris said.

"That statement conflicts with three earlier adjustments."

"Then write me a terrible review."

Gorilla tried a second note, more gently. Eris answered with two quick taps. Bot offered a low steady tone. Madger drummed the tabletop until Eris pointed him toward a spare practice board.

They found four beats that could live beside one another. The fifth refused. Gorilla almost stopped to fix it, then saw his sister watching him.

He played it again. This time everyone left room for the wrong sound.

When the worker from earlier returned for his forgotten coat, he stood in the doorway smiling. Gorilla held out the second mallet.

"You can tell us when it's bad," he said.

"It's bad now."

"Good. You're qualified."

At closing time the damaged runner remained damaged, safely tagged for the morning shift. The instrument remained out of tune. Gorilla wrote his name on the next voluntary repair slot, asked Eris whether that day suited her, and waited for the answer.

Before they left, she struck the plugged rail with one knuckle. A clean little note rose from it.

He had spent the whole visit trying to repair the wrong thing. For once, he did not rush to turn that discovery into another job. He stood beside his sister and listened until the note was gone.

companion_stories.placement: An unnumbered Latchford journey interlude after the pilot and before Sela's rescue-funding secret becomes public. The ordinary delay resolves here; no new attack or villain reveal is added.
companion_stories.text:
Snow saw Asha before Madger did. Her ears rose, her paws quickened, and the pink tag at her collar began its bright little rhythm.

Madger let the lead slacken. Asha was waiting just inside the Six Roads Inn with one hand on the gear rack and the other held low. Snow pressed her nose into that hand, then leaned her whole warm side against Asha's knees.

"There you are," Asha said.

For one foolish second, Madger felt like someone carrying a parcel to its proper address.

Asha looked up. "You too. Don't stand in the rain trying to become dramatic."

The common room smelled of onions, bread and wet traveling cloaks. Six tables bore destination cards. None was named for the person who had paid the most. Asha had saved places at the Stonewake table, including one beside her with a folded blue napkin.

"Who's that for?" Gorilla asked.

"A driver from the late wagon."

Bot checked the ordinary clock above the ledger stand. "The board records arrival before supper."

"The board is optimistic," Asha said. "It has never changed a wheel."

Sela came in carrying the smell of the arrival yard on her coat. She set a damp route slip beside the correction ledger.

"Last scheduled wagon is in. We can clear the place."

Asha began lowering a pot from the serving cart. Her wrist stopped halfway through the movement. Madger reached for it, but she nodded toward Gorilla.

"Both handles. Slowly."

He followed the instruction and set it down where she pointed. Asha flexed her hand once, annoyed rather than ashamed, and carried on serving.

"The place can wait," she told Sela.

"I can pay for the bowl."

"That isn't the part I'm waiting for."

Madger watched Snow settle beneath the side table. The mat was familiar to her. So was the small pause Asha made before dropping a scrap into the proper bowl. Snow did not need to be reminded.

He wondered how many things she remembered that he did not know how to ask about.

Across the table, Sela turned the route slip over. The final line was blank.

"No report means they may have turned back."

"May have," Bot repeated.

Sela gave him a tired look. "I know what the words mean."

"Then perhaps they should stay on the board."

The room quieted by a small degree. Around them, ordinary supper continued: a traveler asking for salt, a chair catching a floor seam, someone at another table describing a hill as if he had personally invented it.

Sela had spent years making decisions before all the facts arrived. Often that was the job. She disliked being told that waiting could also be work.

"I'll check the yard again," Madger said.

Asha pointed to his untouched bowl. "Eat first. The steward is already checking. You don't have to turn every uncertainty into a personal expedition."

Gorilla hid a smile in his cup. He knew the temptation to turn every small problem into a test of strength.

Snow lifted her head. A buckle tapped twice beyond the doorway, followed by a wheel striking the raised threshold stone outside. Her ears turned toward the sound. Asha gave a quiet familiar cue, and Snow stayed on the mat.

The late driver arrived carrying a broken iron fitting. His coat was muddy to the elbows. Behind him, the yard steward held the matching piece.

"Wheel bracket," the driver said. "Borrowed a cart. Borrowed the wrong cart first. Made a very complete tour of the western yard."

Asha unfolded the blue napkin.

There was no ambush, no coded message and no dramatic stranger hidden behind the driver. There was simply a person who had been missing from a record because a piece of metal had failed.

Sela rose to make room. The driver thanked her for keeping his seat. She almost accepted the thanks without correcting it.

"Asha kept it," she said.

It was a small sentence. Nobody applauded.

After supper, Sela returned to the ledger stand. The innkeeper offered a fresh page, but she drew one line through the premature entry so it could still be read. Below it she wrote the arrival time, the bracket failure and the steward's name. Then she signed her own.

Bot did not comment. He had been asked to help count cups, and for once he counted cups.

At the side table, Madger watched Asha scratch the familiar place behind Snow's ear.

"She remembers everything here."

"Some things. She also remembers the cupboard where I kept biscuits, which is unfortunate because the innkeeper keeps cleaning cloths there now."

"Was she happier on the routes?"

Asha stopped scratching. Snow nudged the hand until it resumed.

"She liked the routes. She likes your home. Those aren't enemies."

Madger looked down at the lead looped loosely beside his chair.

"I thought—"

"I know. People do it too. They ask a new home to prove the old one never mattered."

Snow rose, crossed to Madger and investigated the bread smell on his fingers. After a moment she went back to Asha for another scratch. Her answer was inconveniently ordinary.

When the lamps were lowered, Asha asked Gorilla to lift the empty pot onto the cart. She asked Madger to bring her visiting bag to the office. She asked Sela for the date of the next easy convoy, not the fastest one. Each request was specific enough that someone could answer it.

Outside, the rain had stopped. Snow waited at the south entrance while Madger fastened the lead. Asha touched the pink collar gently and stepped back.

Snow looked toward her, then toward the open doorway, then followed Madger's familiar walking cue. A little way down the covered arcade she stopped to smell a post that had apparently acquired urgent news.

Madger waited.

Behind them, Asha carried the folded mat to the store instead of leaving it beneath an empty table. She would put it out when Snow visited again.

Sela passed the ledger on her way to the stairs. Her correction remained visible beneath the original line. She stopped, read both, and left them there.

production_rules: Edition 3.0 geometry and the earlier detailed Burrow plans remain authoritative. These thirteen furnished sheets cover ground floors only.
No new hero designs or voices. Use the approved character cards. Snow has ordinary canine behavior and no speech; Bot has mechanical optics and face.
The pilot stays wholly inside the Burrow. Exterior scenes in this volume belong to later, unnumbered story opportunities.
Scene seeds and complete stories are authored options, not events already added to the dated episode ledger. Local histories and normal-day interior dressing are additive writer canon.

Painted panels establish materials and atmosphere. Their perspective openings, decorative arches and ceiling exaggeration are not construction dimensions. Furnished plans and JSON determine actual rooms and placements.
Portable props can be moved deliberately within a shot sequence. Record state changes and reset them; do not generate unrelated room arrangements from frame to frame.
Keep a stable body drawing for dialogue. Animate approved mouth shapes, blinks and intentional gesture changes. These are set assets, not an interpolated video or a finished episode.
Fictional set and game-blockout plans only; no construction engineering certification is implied.
